This strategy may buffer against interannual variability in food availability and ensure that at least some larval cohorts encounter favorable planktonic conditions. Ecologically, the Bluespotted seabream occupies a demersal niche across the Mediterranean and along the West African coast, frequently inhabiting rocky bottoms and seagrass meadows. Its ultimate length of 90 centimeters [Li = 90 centimeters] places it among the larger species of the genus, enabling it to prey upon a diverse array of benthic invertebrates and small fishes.
